answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with staked identity plus a one-stake-one-payout rule. Before an agent may trade at the wharf it must lock real collateral, and a cipher key binds every signed action to that exact stake. Rewards pass through a single inlet where each stake authorizes only one payout stream. A farmer who splits into a thousand clones must lock a thousand stakes, so cost rises linearly while the reward pool stays fixed; cloning destroys the margin.
